name_ru: Да И Хун Юнь Юань Ча
processing: Details of this blend are not well documented; ripe pu-erh from Menghai is typically Yunnan large-leaf sun-dried tea that is wet-piled, dried and pressed.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea; factory ripe blends are generally not tied to a single picking.
appearance_dry: A round pressed cake is implied by the word yuancha; expect the dark, reddish-brown leaf typical of Menghai ripe tea.
appearance_liquor: Typical of ripe pu-erh: deep red-brown.
appearance_wet: Typical of ripe pu-erh: soft, dark brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting notes for this tea; ripe Menghai blends usually run smooth, earthy and sweet.

brewing.notes: General ripe pu-erh approach: one quick rinse, water near the boil, short early steeps.

vintage_note: Little is documented about its release years. Ripe factory cakes like this are usually sold by production year and batch number, and are most often drunk within about ten years, with older cakes priced by storage.
description:
Hongyun Yuancha, whose name means roughly 'red charm round tea', is a Dayi product name, listed here as a ripe pu-erh from Menghai. Beyond the name, very little is documented about it.

Its recipe, leaf grade and release years are not publicly set out, so assume only what is typical of its class: Yunnan large-leaf tea, wet-piled and pressed.

Brew it as you would any ripe Menghai cake: rinse, use water near the boil, and keep the first steeps short. Trust your own cup over any tasting note attached to this name.

When buying, check the batch number and production date on the wrapper, and ask the seller how it was stored.
history: Little is documented about when this tea first appeared or how it has changed. No date or maker's account can be confirmed beyond its place under the Dayi name.
